'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Cambodia–Thailand relations]]
**A [[Cambodia]]n [[Royal Cambodian Armed Forces|soldier]] is killed in an exchange of fire with a [[Thailand|Thai]] [[Royal Thai Armed Forces|soldier]]. Cambodia initially said that the Thai soldier opened fire, but Thailand denied this citing a misunderstanding when the Cambodian soldier crossed the border during a routine operation. [https://apnews.com/article/thailand-cambodia-soldiers-border-clash-a4b8547559ff1fe493bdac60aad008eb (AP)]
**[[Prime Minister of Thailand|Thai prime minister]] [[Paetongtarn Shinawatra]] says that she spoke with [[Prime Minister of Cambodia|Cambodian prime minister]] [[Hun Manet]], and both agreed to resolve the crisis. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-05-28/thai-cambodian-soldiers-exchange-fire-at-disputed-border-area (Bloomberg)]
*[[New Cold War]]
**More than two million documents related to Russian military procurement from a public database for contractors are published, including information on the modernization and build-up of the [[Strategic Rocket Forces|Russian Strategic Missile Forces]], [[Dombarovsky (air base)|military base at Yasny]], and [[Avangard (hypersonic glide vehicle)|Avangard hypersonic glide vehicle]]. [https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2025/05/28/russias-vast-nuclear-modernization-exposed-in-unprecedented-security-breach-der-spiegel-a89262 (The Moscow Times)] [https://www.newsweek.com/russia-nuclear-spiegel-weapons-2077935 (''Newsweek'')]
*[[Red Sea crisis]]
**[[Israel]] says it launched [[airstrike]]s against targets in [[Houthi-controlled territory of Yemen|Houthi-controlled Yemen]], destroying the last operational plane of [[Yemenia Airlines]] at [[Sanaa International Airport]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/israel-says-it-has-hit-houthi-targets-including-last-plane-sanaa-airport-2025-05-28/ (Reuters)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[Miss Grand International 2024]]
**The reigning [[Miss Grand International]], [[Rachel Gupta]], resigns from her title, citing mistreatment and a toxic environment. The [[Miss Grand International (company)|Miss Grand International Organization]] announces Gupta's termination from the title, citing her failure to fulfill assigned duties and her engagement in external projects without prior approval. [https://mb.com.ph/2025/05/28/miss-grand-international-2024-rachel-gupta-steps-down-promises-to-return-crown (''Manila Bulletin'')]
*[[Namibian genocide]]
**[[Namibia]] commemorates its first [[Genocide]] Remembrance Day to honor the indigenous [[Herero people|Herero]] and [[Nama people|Nama]] peoples who were [[ethnic cleansing|ethnically cleansed]] by the [[German South West Africa]] [[Imperial Schutztruppe for German South West Africa|colonial forces]] as proxy of the [[German Empire]]. [https://apnews.com/article/namibia-germany-genocide-commemoration-indigenous-herero-nama-abe931fbab90756a8717f1e235871e47 (AP)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2025 Blatten glacier collapse]]
**A landslide destroys almost all of the village of [[Blatten (Lötschen)|Blatten]], [[Switzerland]], resulting in one person going missing. [https://www.lenouvelliste.ch/valais/haut-valais/une-grande-partie-du-village-de-blatten-rayee-de-la-carte-on-a-perdu-notre-village-pas-notre-coeur-revivez-notre-direct-1454317 (''Le Nouvelliste'')]
*A boat carrying over 100 [[human migration|migrants]] capsizes within reach of the shores of the [[El Hierro]] island in the [[Spain|Spanish]] [[Canary Islands]]. Four women and three girls are found [[drowning|drowned]], while a [[medical helicopter]] evacuates two other children in critical condition to a nearby hospital. [https://apnews.com/article/migrants-capsized-boat-spain-canary-islands-36d85cd37146306439fdb0947c302b90 (AP)]
*Four people are killed and damage is reported in a [[crowd crush]] and shooting after hundreds of [[Palestinian]]s stormed a [[United Nations]] food warehouse in an attempt to get food in [[Gaza City]], [[Palestine]]. [https://www.pbs.org/newshour/world/1-killed-dozens-wounded-when-crowd-was-fired-upon-at-chaotic-gaza-aid-site-health-officials-say (PBS News)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Corruption in Albania]]
**Former [[President of Albania|Albanian president]] [[Ilir Meta]] is formally charged with [[corruption]], [[money laundering]], [[tax evasion]], and concealing property from authorities. The charges were detailed in a report from anti-corruption prosecutors. Meta was arrested in October. [https://apnews.com/article/albania-corruption-former-president-ilir-meta-charged-8fb2c1d9ab32d9983c2114d6426bb227 (AP)]
*[[Pamplona massacre]]
**The [[Constitutional Government of Timor-Leste]] announces that expelled former [[Philippine]] lawmaker [[Arnolfo Teves Jr.]], the main suspect in the [[Pamplona massacre|assassination]] of [[Negros Oriental]] governor [[Roel Degamo]] in 2023, will be deported back to the Philippines after his arrest by [[Immigration Service of Timor-Leste]]. [https://www.rappler.com/philippines/timor-leste-arrest-arnie-teves-may-2025/ (Rappler)]
*[[Patnagarh bombing]]
**A court in [[Odisha]], [[India]], sentences a man to [[life in prison]] for a 2018 bombing at a [[wedding]] in [[Patnagarh]] that killed two people. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c071myeve25o (BBC News)]
*Five people are killed, including the perpetrator, and four others are injured, including one critically, when a [[drunk]] 17-year-old goes on a [[mass stabbing]] rampage before killing himself in an [[arson]] attack at a house during a birthday party in [[Irkutsk]], [[Irkutsk Oblast]], Russia. [https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2025/05/28/teenager-kills-5-injures-4-in-drunken-stabbing-in-irkutsk-region-a89248 (The Moscow Times)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2025 Australian federal election]]
**The [[National Party of Australia|National Party]] rejoins the [[Opposition (Australia)|Opposition]] [[Liberal-National Coalition|Coalition]] one week after moving to the crossbench. [https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2025/may/28/liberals-and-nationals-reach-agreement-to-reunite-coalition-a-week-after-dramatic-split (''The Guardian'')]
*[[2025 People's Justice Party leadership election]]
**Following their defeats in the [[People's Justice Party (Malaysia)|People's Justice Party]] leadership election, ministers [[Rafizi Ramli]] and [[Nik Nazmi]] announce their intention to resign from the [[Cabinet of Malaysia]]. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/asia/malaysia-economy-minister-rafizi-ramli-ally-nik-nazmi-quit-cabinet-after-losses-ruling-pkrs-leadership-polls-5156601 (CNA)]
*[[Education policy of the second Donald Trump administration]]
**U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio says his department will start revoking visas for Chinese students and increase scrutiny on all future visa applications from China and Hong Kong. [https://apnews.com/article/international-students-visas-trump-guidance-social-media-a1f5180ce83560aff66dd65534906697 (AP)]
*[[Tariffs in the second Trump administration]]
**The [[United States Court of International Trade]] rules that [[President of the United States|President]] [[Donald Trump]] cannot enact sweeping tariffs under the [[International Emergency Economic Powers Act]] without [[US Congress|congressional approval]]. [https://apnews.com/article/trump-tariffs-trade-court-0392dbd59f548e49ad4f64254ae3f94a (AP)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2024–25 UEFA Conference League]]
**In association football, [[Chelsea F.C.]] defeat [[Real Betis]] 4–1 in the [[UEFA Conference League]] [[2025 UEFA Conference League final|final]] at the [[Wrocław Stadium]] in [[Wrocław]], [[Poland]], becoming the first club to win all four current major [[UEFA]] competition trophies. [https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/crk2zx2e1xet#Report (BBC Sport)]
*[[2025 in sumo]]
**In [[sumo]], [[Ōnosato Daiki]] is promoted and becomes the sport's 75th ''[[yokozuna]]''. Ōnosato reached the highest rank of ''yokozuna'' faster than anyone in the modern history of [[sumo]], achieving the promotion in 13 tournaments and never posting a losing record during a tournament. [https://english.kyodonews.net/news/2025/05/68e4a493f74c-update1-sumo-onosato-becomes-yokozuna-at-record-pace-after-13-tournaments.html (Kyodo News)]
